finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /profile/avatar makes a server-side GET to an attacker-supplied URL. The only check is a https:// prefix test, and axios follows redirects by default, so a 302 to internal hosts or 169.254.169.254 bypasses it. The response length is returned as bytes, giving a size oracle.

trace.note: typeof string and startsWith("https://") only; scheme/prefix check, no host allowlist
axios.get(url) with default redirect following, no re-validation per hop
res.json({ bytes: img.data.length }) leaks body length to caller

finding.guards_checked: Scheme prefix check at server.js:11 (does not close SSRF). No host allowlist, no RFC-1918/loopback/link-local/metadata IP blocking, no maxRedirects=0 or per-hop re-validation, no DNS-rebinding pinning, no auth observed on the route. Redirect behavior of axios is from default library behavior, not executed. Semgrep not run (no shell tool). Severity HIGH retained due to size oracle and internal host users.internal:8080 referenced in same file; validation tier 1.

verdict.guard_found: Only a scheme-prefix check at server.js:11 (`typeof url !== "string" || !url.startsWith("https://")`). It is a prefix check, not a host allowlist, so it does not close the finding. No auth middleware on the route (server.js:9), no maxRedirects=0, no private-IP or metadata-address blocking, and no per-hop re-validation before axios.get at server.js:14.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the file: req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10) is attacker-controlled on an unauthenticated route (server.js:9), the only check is the https:// prefix (server.js:11), and axios.get (server.js:14) runs with no host restriction, so the server makes a request to any host the attacker names, and the response length is returned at server.js:15.
